continuities.name: Baahubali (films, animated series, prequel novels)
continuities.description: One continuity: the two Rajamouli films (and their re-edit), the two animated prequel series and Anand Neelakantan's prequel novel trilogy. Wikipedia frames every one of these as part of the franchise and as prequels to the films. No absolute in-universe years are given anywhere, so the order is relative only.
continuities.quote: S. S. Rajamouli approached Indian novelist Anand Neelakantan to write a prequel trilogy of novels for the Baahubali film franchise. … The series serves as a prologue to Baahubali: The Beginning and Baahubali 2: The Conclusion. … Set before the events of the films, this prequel follows Baahubali and Bhallaladeva
continuities.note: Wikipedia never says whether the novels, The Lost Legends and Crown of Blood agree with one another; each is only tied to the films. Kept in one continuity per the instruction (Wikipedia ties the novels to the film continuity); a stricter reading would split the tie-ins into their own continuities.

continuities.name: KGF
continuities.description: Prashanth Neel's KGF film series (Chapter 1 and Chapter 2), set in the Kolar Gold Fields from 1951 to 1981, with a present-day frame narration.
continuities.quote: KGF is an Indian Kannada-language period action film series set mostly in the Kolar Gold Fields, which gives the series its name, created by Prashanth Neel and produced by Hombale Films

continuities.name: Salaar
continuities.description: Salaar: Part 1 – Ceasefire (Part 2 not yet released). Kept separate from KGF: Wikipedia does not state that the films share a universe.
continuities.quote: The film's initial storyline was pitched from Neel's 2014 Kannada-language debut film Ugramm and is the maiden part of a two-part film.
continuities.note: Shared-universe speculation is not recorded as fact on Wikipedia. The closest statements are producer Vijay Kiragandur's ambition in the KGF series article ("Going forward, we are going to create a Marvel kind of universe. We want to bring different characters from different movies and create something like Doctor Strange.") and the Salaar article's reception note on "similarities with Ugramm and KGF". Neither says the films share a continuity, so they are not merged and no link is recorded.

titles.title: K.G.F: Chapter 1

units.label: Film
units.release_quote: | released = {{Film date|df=yes|2018|12|20|United States, Canada|2018|12|21|India}} … The first installment, Chapter 1, was released on 21 December 2018
units.note: India date used. The film's lead says "The Kannada version of K.G.F: Chapter 1 was released on 20 December 2018 and the dubbed versions … released the next day" (marked citation needed). The infobox gives 20 December only for the United States and Canada and 21 December for India, and the series article gives 21 December 2018.

in_universe.label: 1951–1978 (frame: present day)
in_universe.quote: Journalist Anand Ingalagi's controversial book El Dorado, which documents the history of the Kolar Gold Fields (K.G.F.) from 1951 to 2018 … 1951, Raja "Rocky" Krishnappa Bairya is born to Shanti … Prashant explains about the setting of the film in 1970–80, stating, "… So, 1978 was the perfect setting for us, because the higher the price of gold, the higher the greed of men."
in_universe.note: The 1951 start is stated in the plot. The 1978 end comes from the director's production quote about the setting, not from the plot, so the range is inferred. The framing interview is present day; the book covers events up to 2018.

titles.notes: Article title is now "KGF: Chapter 1"; the on-screen title is "K.G.F: Chapter 1" (title redirect).

in_universe.label: c. 1978–1981 (frame: present day)
in_universe.quote: In 1981, Ramika Sen wins the Indian general election and becomes Prime Minister. … In a mid-credits scene set three months before Rocky's death, CIA agent John Booker delivers Ramika Sen a classified file detailing Rocky's criminal activities across the United States and sixteen other countries between 1978 and 1981.
in_universe.note: 1981 is stated. The start is inferred: the film picks up straight after Chapter 1 (c. 1978), and the mid-credits file covers Rocky's activities "between 1978 and 1981".

titles.notes: Chapter 2 ends teasing "K.G.F: Chapter 3"; the series article says it "might start filming only in 2028 for a release in 2029". Not released, so not included.
